findings.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION
findings.rationale: The cap is mutual, but it is limited to amounts paid for the single "transaction which the liability relates to", which is materially less than 12 months' fees and can fall below our 6-month floor. The only carve-out is Section 8 (IP indemnity); confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud all sit inside the cap, so the clause fails our fallback.

replacement.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
replacement.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8, ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 10, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IS NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the cap to 12 months' fees paid or payable rather than the fees for a single transaction, and added the standard carve-outs so that indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud sit outside the cap.

findings.quote: Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
findings.rationale: Vendor gives a full IP defence and indemnity covering us and our Customers, with the usual exclusions (use outside documentation, third-party modification) and procure/modify/refund remedies, and it is carved out of the liability cap entirely. This meets the fallback; we note only that it does not extend to Vendor's breach of law, data incidents or wilful misconduct.

findings.quote: "CORIO MARKET SEGMENT" means those customers with annual sales revenues of less than $1,000,000,000.
findings.rationale: The licence is confined to the "Corio Market Segment" and to North America, which operates as a field-of-use/territory restriction on the customers we may serve with this product. It is framed as licence scope rather than a covenant, and Section 2.10 gives a path to worldwide expansion with consent not unreasonably withheld, so we flag it for commercial confirmation rather than redline.

findings.quote: nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement)
findings.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds us; the only directional restrictions (Vendor not contacting our Customers for non-ASP sales and referring them back to us) run in our favour.
No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation is imposed on us anywhere in the Agreement or Exhibit B.

findings.quote: Commerce One covenants that during the term of this Agreement, it will continue to require all Commerce One employees, agents, contractors or consultants to sign an Employee NDA/Invention Agreement
findings.rationale: There is no non-solicitation or no-hire restriction binding us, which is our preferred position.

findings.quote: The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years.
findings.rationale: We are locked into a five-year initial term with termination available only for uncured material breach or insolvency; there is no convenience right for us. Our playbook treats the absence of a customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months as a deviation.

replacement.oldText: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
replacement.newText: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement. In addition, Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) (or, at Commerce One's election, sixty (60)) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund any prepaid fees covering the period after the effective date of termination.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to a five-year term with no exit; we have added a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund. We can live with 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

findings.quote: this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration
findings.rationale: Renewal terms are 12 months with a 30-day non-renewal window, which meets our preferred position. We note only the absence of a renewal reminder and a cap on price uplift at renewal.

findings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA
findings.rationale: California law with AAA arbitration seated in San Francisco sits at our fallback: California is an accepted jurisdiction and the arbitration is domestic, not a foreign seat. We would prefer courts over mandatory arbitration but do not redline on that alone.

findings.quote: either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent
findings.rationale: The assignment clause is mutual and carries an M&A/asset-sale carve-out, and there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, so it sits at the fallback. We note the consent standard for other assignments is not expressed as "not to be unreasonably withheld" and that the competitor exception cuts both ways.

findings.quote: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
findings.rationale: Interface code created solely by us flips to Vendor ownership merely because Vendor supports it on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us. That is an assignment of our IP to the Vendor and falls in walk-away territory; the deferred negotiation over ownership of enhancements developed solely by us compounds the exposure.

replacement.oldText: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
replacement.newText: shall be owned by Corio. Where such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One, Commerce One shall have a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use such Developments solely to provide that support, but shall acquire no ownership rights, including
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We own what we build; Vendor supporting our interface code should not transfer ownership of it. We have replaced the ownership flip with a support-purpose licence to Vendor.

findings.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license
findings.rationale: The licence is perpetual and irrevocable, permits unlimited sublicensing to our Customers, and is transferable to a successor via Section 14.1; Section 14.8 preserves our right to subcontract delivery. Affiliates are not expressly named, which we would add if convenient, but the grant meets the fallback.

findings.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
findings.rationale: Audits are annual, by an independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, with no access to our systems. This meets our preferred position; only the notice period is "reasonable" rather than a fixed 30 days.

findings.quote: Maintenance and Support Fees: Net 30 of Software acceptance anniversary date, and each year thereafter.
findings.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination charges are payable by us under the Agreement or Exhibit B.

findings.quote: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
findings.rationale: The warranty runs from the Effective Date and expires no later than 31 December 1999, which is effectively the acceptance date under Section 3.1 — so the conformance warranty lapses at or immediately after go-live and falls short of the 90-day fallback. The remedies (correct, replace, refund on termination) are acceptable.

replacement.oldText: for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period")
replacement.newText: for a period of ninety (90) days from Corio's acceptance of the Software pursuant to Section 3.1 (the "Warranty Period")
replacement.comment: [Playbook] A warranty that expires on the acceptance date gives us no protection; we have run the 90-day period from acceptance in line with our standard position.

findings.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance obligation, although Vendor hosts the MarketSite.net Service and places personnel alongside our teams. We ask for a standard short insurance paragraph in the miscellaneous section.

replacement.oldText: as set forth in Section 365(n) of the Code.
replacement.newText:
as set forth in Section 365(n) of the Code.

14.11 Insurance. Commerce One shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Commerce One shall provide certificates of insurance on request.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We require standard insurance from vendors that host services and process our data; we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

findings.quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party
findings.rationale: Survival of the licence, support and the source-code escrow give us useful continuity, but there is no transition-assistance obligation and no obligation on Vendor to return our and our Customers' data from the MarketSite.net Service in a usable format. We ask for the standard exit paragraph.

replacement.oldText: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
replacement.newText: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers. In addition, upon expiration or termination for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Corio all Corio and Customer data in its possession in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We need our data back and help moving on exit; we can accept 90 days of transition assistance as a fallback.

findings.quote: No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
findings.rationale: There is no take-or-pay or shortfall commitment on us; the 40-user figure is a threshold within the revenue-share mechanic and the Exhibit D customer-order target is expressly non-binding. The recurring annual fees over the five-year term are addressed under our termination-for-convenience point.
